title: Pick the cryptographic tool for each requirement
scenario: Each requirement below comes from a real system design review. Drop it into the tool that meets it. Several tools sound as if they would help with most of these; only one actually provides what each requirement asks for.
requirements: Every requirement goes in exactly one column.
Ask what the requirement needs: to detect change, to hide content, to prove origin, to slow guessing, or to keep a value out of the system.

items.label: Detect whether a downloaded installer was altered
Store passwords so the server never needs to recover them
Make two users with the same password store different values
Make every password guess cost an attacker a tenth of a second
Encrypt a two terabyte backup quickly
Prove the finance director approved a contract and it has not changed since
Stop a sender from later denying they sent a message
Let a shop process card payments without storing card numbers

subtasks.correctNote: Compare the file's hash with the published one. Nothing needs to be hidden, only checked for change.
A hash is one way. Encryption would mean a key that can recover every password, which is exactly what must not exist.
A unique salt per user makes identical passwords produce different stored values.
Key stretching makes each guess deliberately expensive. Salt does nothing to the cost of a single guess.
Symmetric ciphers are fast enough for bulk data. Asymmetric encryption is used to exchange the key, not to encrypt terabytes.
A signature proves who signed and that the content has not changed since. A hash alone proves no identity.
Only the holder of the private key could have produced the signature, which is non-repudiation.
A token stands in for the card number and is useless on its own; the real number lives with the payment provider.
